question: What type of cartilage covers the ends of bones inside a synovial joint?
explanation: Hyaline cartilage provides a smooth, slippery surface that helps absorb shock and reduce friction during joint movement. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h1)

question: Which structure directly secretes synovial fluid into the joint cavity?
explanation: The inner layer of the articular capsule, called the synovial membrane, produces the slippery fluid that nourishes and lubricates the joint. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h1)

question: What is the primary function of a bursa in a synovial joint?

options.A: To anchor bone ends tightly together
options.B: To supply blood directly to cartilage cells
options.C: To produce new synovial fluid daily
options.D: To reduce friction between moving body parts

explanation: Bursae are fluid-filled sacs that cushion areas where tendons, ligaments, and bones rub against each other. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h2)

question: Why are menisci important in joints like the knee?

options.A: They connect muscle bellies directly to the bone shaft
options.B: They replace the need for synovial fluid production
options.C: They help irregular bone surfaces fit together better
options.D: They allow the joint to move in all possible directions

explanation: Menisci are fibrocartilage discs that improve the fit between articulating bones, helping distribute weight and absorb shock. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h2)

question: Which type of synovial joint allows for movement in all axes, including rotation?
explanation: The spherical head fitting into a cuplike socket gives ball-and-socket joints the greatest range of motion in multiple directions. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h3)

question: A patient is moving their elbow back and forth in a single plane. Which joint shape makes this movement possible?
explanation: Hinge joints operate like a door hinge, allowing movement in only one plane, such as bending and straightening the elbow. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h3)

question: What term describes moving a limb toward the midline of the body?
explanation: Adduction brings a body part toward the central axis of the body, whereas abduction moves it away. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h4)

question: Why is circumduction considered a combination of movements?

options.A: It changes the angle of the joint without moving the limb
options.B: It turns the bone purely along its own single longitudinal axis
options.C: It requires both shoulders and hips to move at the exact same time
options.D: It involves sequential flexion, abduction, extension, and adduction

explanation: Circumduction is a compound movement where the distal end of a limb traces a circle while the proximal end stays relatively stationary. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h4)

question: Which condition is primarily characterized by the autoimmune inflammation of the synovial membrane?
explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis is a systemic autoimmune disease where the body attacks its own synovial membranes, causing pain and swelling. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h5)

question: A pregnant woman presents with joint pain caused by the breakdown of protective hyaline cartilage from normal wear and tear. Which diagnosis fits best?
explanation: Osteoarthritis involves the progressive degeneration of articular cartilage over time, often exacerbated by weight and mechanical stress. [learn more](BMP111_U2_T16#BMP111_U2_T16_h5)
